source_cards.title: Learning Input-Channel Permutation Equivariance for Multi-Channel Source Separation: Reducing Bleeding in Small Music Ensembles
key_findings: The same random permutation is applied to input and target channels; output identity remains tied to the input channel and this is not PIT.
Permutation training strongly improved objective SDR generalization to unseen rooms, layouts, distances and instruments in the reported five-channel string-ensemble setup.
At 25 cm on unseen URMP strings, magnitude plus permutation achieved 5.3 dB mean SDR improvement versus 0.3 dB without permutation; real-imaginary plus permutation achieved 3.9 dB versus -5.5 dB.
The magnitude spectral branch outperformed concatenated real-imaginary features in this architecture; this does not establish that phase cues are generally unhelpful.
limitations: Synthetic acoustic training and evaluation conditions.
Strings and small ensembles rather than live rock drums.
Objective SDR without a listening test.

source_cards.title: The Spheres Dataset: Multitrack Orchestral Recordings for Music Source Separation and Information Retrieval
source_cards.publication: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing 34 (2026), 2622-2634
key_findings: Isolated performances were captured through all active microphones, enabling exact target and bleed contribution matrices.
The public record lists 23 microphones, 48 kHz lossless FLAC, stereo mixes, multichannel signals, RIRs and raw clap-sweep recordings.
Within-dataset separation improvements did not transfer reliably to Operation Beethoven; room, microphone and instrument mismatch caused artifacts and interference degradation.
Similar-timbre violin sections were a difficult case.
source_cards.license_note: Zenodo labels the record Open but the Rights/License field is blank; article-text licensing and public-domain compositions do not establish the recording license.
limitations: Individually recorded lines rather than simultaneous ensemble performance.
No listener test connecting SDR/SIR/SAR to mix quality.

knowledge_cards.claim: Joint input-target permutation is an equivariance augmentation, not PIT; output remains tied to the corresponding input microphone.
A multichannel debleeder needs a reorder-then-unreorder test to expose channel-index shortcuts.
Room, layout, distance and instrument domain shift can reverse per-channel benefit even when training metrics are positive.
A weaker complex spectral branch in one dual-domain model is not evidence that phase information is generally unnecessary.
Exact target-bleed-RIR matrices validate separation mechanics but do not define the artistic target for rock close microphones.
SDR and SIR must remain separate from SAR, transient integrity, inter-channel timing, room image and listener preference.
Snare top-bottom and multi-kick polarity decisions require whole-kit context rather than a fixed always-flip rule.
Finite keyed ducking or expansion and tuned de-essing are candidates before hard gating when bleed is path-specific.
Visual peak alignment may increase fullness while changing intentional overhead-room arrival; geometry, mono and depth controls are required.

rule_candidates.when_apply: training or evaluating a joint multichannel debleeder
rule_candidates.change: train with paired input-target permutations and run reorder-unreorder inference tests
rule_candidates.proposed_range: all permutations for small P or a fixed representative sample
rule_candidates.success: reordered and restored outputs agree within documented tolerances and perceptual ranking is stable
rule_candidates.cancel: output role or audible result depends on channel index

rule_candidates.when_apply: model is proposed for unseen room layout distance instrument or channel count
rule_candidates.change: hold out each claimed generalization axis and compare raw simple and learned baselines
rule_candidates.proposed_range: at least one holdout per claimed axis
rule_candidates.success: positive per-channel results and stable blind preference on holdout
rule_candidates.cancel: critical channel degrades or artifacts appear

rule_candidates.change: retain SDR SIR SAR ISR transient timing room and listening as separate outputs
rule_candidates.success: isolation rises without fidelity or preference loss

rule_candidates.when_apply: opposed snare top-bottom or distance-separated kick microphones
rule_candidates.instrument_section: full drum kit and full mix by section
rule_candidates.change: compare unchanged and both polarity orientations; test delay separately
rule_candidates.proposed_range: two polarity states per channel; no universal delay
rule_candidates.success: target role improves consistently after loudness matching
rule_candidates.cancel: solo benefit disappears in kit mix or mono room worsens

rule_candidates.when_apply: snare spill dominates a kick batter attack mic
rule_candidates.instrument_section: kick and snare events including coincident hits
rule_candidates.change: compare bypass manual edit hard gate and snare-keyed finite attenuation
rule_candidates.proposed_range: event-tuned attenuation and ballistics; no source numbers
rule_candidates.success: less snare spill without losing required kick event
rule_candidates.cancel: coincident hits are cut or processing is more audible than bleed

rule_candidates.when_apply: snare-bottom is useful but between-hit bleed is excessive
rule_candidates.instrument_section: snare normal hits ghost notes and fills
rule_candidates.change: key finite expansion from snare-top and compare bypass manual and hard gate
rule_candidates.success: bleed falls without loss of quiet articulation or decay
rule_candidates.cancel: ghost notes decay or detector reliability fails

rule_candidates.when_apply: hi-hat bleed dominates a snare or tom close mic and hard gating damages envelope
rule_candidates.instrument_section: close drum mic across normal hits ghost notes fills and cymbal-dense sections
rule_candidates.change: test tuned de-esser or dynamic band after bypass and manual baselines
rule_candidates.proposed_range: source-specific frequency and depth; no source numbers
rule_candidates.success: hi-hat distraction falls without loss of drum identity
rule_candidates.cancel: lisping splash modulation or dull attack appears

experiments.title: Snare spill control in kick attack mic

handoff: Test multichannel debleeders under channel reorder and room-layout-instrument holdouts; do not let SDR or SIR replace fidelity, room and blind preference. For rock drums audition polarity states in the full kit and mix rather than always flipping the bottom mic. Treat snare-keyed finite ducking or expansion and tuned de-essing as candidates before hard gating, with coincident-hit and ghost-note cancellation checks.
